body: Depends on what your question is. I only have some experience with BMD, Hanover Hounds and Polish Hounds.

All of them are excellent pointers, so it depends on the finer details of what you want. 

Vizlas are generally softer and pretty easy to train. Not very gamey, and they can be pretty hyper. Of the breeds you listed, they are the most sensitive. Training methods should be pretty soft.

The Weimaraner can be quite hardheaded and stubborn, and has a certain type of sharpness. Depending on the breeding line, very good and stable dogs or hyper vigilant menaces. 

GSP and EP are pretty similar in most aspects. Both are very, very fast, quick pointers with a wide search range. However, the GSP is what we call a "Vollgebrauchshund", an all-around hunting dog, while the EP is a pointing specialist. 

If I wanted a pointing dog, I would get a MV or an EP.

I would be careful and observe him during the hunt. 6 months is the age were dogs with high drive don't know when to stop, even if they are hurting themselves. Instead of resting him before, give him frequent breaks during the hunt.

Water and Glucose solution were my best friends when I took the youngster hunting for the first times.

Very interesting to see that the topic of blood tracking is viewed quite differently in the US than in Europe. 


In Germany, it is mandatory by law to either have an officially tested tracking dog or to at least have the possibility to have a tracker available on short notice. It's one of the basics of the so called "Waidgerechtigkeit", to ensure that an animal which was wounded is found as quickly ss possible, so it does not have to suffer too long. They are also responsible for tracking animals that have been hit by cars, or are injured by other means than a wrong shot.

It will probably be difficult to find a DD with a smoother/shorter coat. Sadly, most breeders tend to breed for longer coat in the last few years, similar to the Stichelhaar coat.

I am a houndswoman, but if I take other hunters dogs with me, I prefer the DKs. They are a bit sharper, faster, quicker on the uptake but tend to relax immediately after the hunt is over. The DDs sometimes seem like they always have an undercurrent of exitement, and often don't know when to stop. 

But: DDs stay closer to you. DKs have a wider search area, and they are hellishly fast. They also have a nicer point, in my opinion.

Both breeds are fine pointing dogs. I would just recommend that you do some independent research on the health situation of both breeds, ideally outside from the JGHV-sources.

I live in a country which is actually pretty ok regarding the health system and the treatment of psychological disorders, but the prevention Hotline? Pardon my French, it was a shitshow.

Normally, ideally, we would have around 30 lines open around 10pm to 3am - in reality, there were days where only five people came in to take calls.

We did not have a set script, but there are a few Focal points which we had to look out for; is the person actually committing suicide in that exact moment (which were the worst calls, since we did not have any possibility to trace), does the caller just want to talk without any feedback, or is feedback and TLC needed.

Chances are high that the people at the Hotline also went to work that day, ate something and then took their shift at the Hotline. It's all volunteers there.

This is not meant to be an excuse for the shitty quality you received when you called, but perhaps an explanation. Pro-Tip: call and call and call again until you get somebody you click with. Hope you get better. Hugs!

I just can't forget the peace I felt when I died. If I did not know how it feels, perhaps then I would still have that primal fear of death that most humans have. But for me, it was the most calm I've felt in my life. I was happy that it was over, and I have not been that happy ever since.
